feature1.prompt: ImageField unnecessarily adds a post_init signal handler to the model. While debugging performance issues in a Django application, it was discovered that a significant amount of time is spent initializing models due to the unconditional connection of a post_init signal handler. The signal handler is effectively a no-op when width_field and height_field are not set, and its unconditional addition leads to needless processing. The goal of this feature is to modify the behavior so that the post_init signal is only connected when either width_field or height_field is provided, thereby improving initialization performance.
feature1.hint_texts: Focus on the contribute_to_class method in django/db/models/fields/files.py. Update the condition that connects the post_init signal so that it only does so when the model is non-abstract and at least one of width_field or height_field is set. Ensure that the signal handler is not connected unnecessarily when the dimension fields are not in use.
feature1.entrypoint: File: django/db/models/fields/files.py, Function: contribute_to_class. Look around the area where the post_init signal is connected (approximately line 441) and update the conditional to include a check for self.width_field or self.height_field.

feature2.prompt: ImageField unnecessarily adds a post_init signal handler to the model. The signal handler, which is a no-op when width_field and height_field are not set, reveals that parts of the internal image dimension update logic are redundant. Because these dimension fields are not actually used, the extra conditional checks in the update process contribute to unnecessary processing. This feature aims to simplify the internal update mechanism by removing the redundant check, ensuring that only relevant operations are performed during model initialization.
feature2.hint_texts: Work in the update_dimension_fields method in django/db/models/fields/files.py. Remove the redundant check for the presence of dimension fields (width_field or height_field) and simplify the conditional logic so that the method only checks whether the field is deferred. This will clean up the code and contribute to overall performance improvements.
feature2.entrypoint: File: django/db/models/fields/files.py, Function: update_dimension_fields. Identify and remove the code block that sets and checks a variable (e.g., has_dimension_fields) to determine the presence of width_field or height_field, retaining only the check for whether the field is deferred (i.e., if self.attname is present in instance.__dict__).
